primary_topics: Anniversary message at the 30th Anniversary of the Metrobank Foundation, January 22, 2009 -- invited by Dr. George S.K. Ty; CJP as senior adviser to Metrobank and Vice-Chair of its Foundation Board of Advisers
Trust as the one word that describes Dr. George Ty: told to a journalist at a wedding reception about a year before; in times of financial meltdown and cratered confidence, trust is what people seek

Excellence as the common thread of all Metrobank Foundation programs: 'it seeks, aspires for, bathes in and promotes excellence all the time, everywhere'; God-given natural talent as the foundation of each person's obligation to discover and develop their gifts
The good-news-bad-news parable (Middle Ages version) applied to the Metrobank Foundation context: in good and bad times, persevere and keep doing your best
sub_topics: CJP's dual role: invited by Dr. Ty to be senior adviser to Metrobank after retirement; also Vice-Chair of the Board of Advisers of the Metrobank Foundation

Trust as the one-word descriptor: at a wedding reception about a year ago, a journalist asked what one word best describes Dr. Ty; CJP replied without hesitation: 'Trust'; 'in these days of uncertainties, of financial meltdowns and of cratered confidence in institutions and personalities in our country and in the world, what we all look up to is a person who does what he says, who takes care of our concerns more than he does of his own'

Excellence as the governing Foundation philosophy: 'excellence drives the entire philosophy of the Metrobank Foundation. It seeks, aspires for, bathes in and promotes excellence all the time, everywhere... year in and year out, amongst its officers and employees, inside among its affiliates and partners, and brings it outside to the community, the nation and the world'

Excellence demands best performance: 'not everyone has been endowed with the same amount of gray matter or artistic talent... But whatever be our situation in life, one thing is sure: God has given each of us, without exception, a natural talent. It is everyone's responsibility to discover and to develop to the maximum whatever natural gift the Lord has endowed us.'

Good-news-bad-news parable (third full telling in the corpus, slight variation): farmer in the Middle Ages, son breaks left leg taming wild horses; kingdom goes to war; all able-bodied conscripted; kingdom loses; all young men killed; 'Friends, like our farmer, we are constantly besieged by events outside our control. Let us not be frustrated, let us not give up... let us persevere, let us continue doing our best, continue to believe in ourselves, continue to work hard for our ultimate victory'

stances.claim: Excellence and Trust are not independent values but mutually reinforcing ones: 'they must go together because they mutually reinforce each other.' In times of financial crisis and cratered confidence (the 2008-2009 global financial meltdown is the implicit backdrop), the Metrobank Foundation's combination of excellence programs and the trust embodied by Dr. Ty is the correct institutional response.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered January 22, 2009 as the anniversary message at the 30th Anniversary of the Metrobank Foundation -- invited by Dr. George S.K. Ty; CJP as senior adviser to Metrobank and Vice-Chair of its Foundation Board of Advisers -- this address opens with the trust-as-one-word anecdote: at a wedding reception about a year earlier, a journalist asked what one word best describes Dr. Ty; CJP replied without hesitation 'Trust.' In the context of the 2008-2009 global financial meltdown and 'cratered confidence in institutions and personalities,' trust is what people seek: 'a person who does what he says, who takes care of our concerns more than he does of his own.' Excellence is the governing Foundation philosophy: 'it seeks, aspires for, bathes in and promotes excellence all the time, everywhere... God has given each of us, without exception, a natural talent. It is everyone's responsibility to discover and to develop to the maximum whatever natural gift the Lord has endowed us.' He tells the good-news-bad-news parable (third telling in the corpus, applied to the Foundation community during the financial crisis): 'like our farmer, we are constantly besieged by events outside our control. Let us not be frustrated, let us not give up... let us persevere.' The 30th Anniversary theme is Excel, Engage, Empower (three Es); 'the beacon and the anchor is the first: EXCEL'; but 'the three Es must be accompanied by the one T that our group chairman is known for, and that is TRUST. EXCELLENCE and TRUST must go together because they mutually reinforce each other. We celebrate Metrobank Foundation's three Es, as in Excel, Engage, Empower, because they are backed up by one T as in George S.K. Ty.'
